# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ibrahim_2026_paclitaxel_rodent"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ibrahim_2026_paclitaxel_rodent"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-026-04053-z> (open access, PMC13179264)

Ibrahim 2026 built a semi-mechanistic PK-PD model in four sequential steps:
a plasma PK model for Cremophor EL (CrEL)-formulated paclitaxel, a PK model of
each paclitaxel-induced peripheral neurotoxicity (PIPN) site (dorsal root
ganglia, DRG; peripheral nerve, PN, represented by sciatic nerve; brain), a
simultaneous fit of all PIPN sites, and finally a neurofilament light chain
(NfL) model in which the tubulin-bound paclitaxel in the PIPN sites drives NfL
leakage into CSF and serum. The final NONMEM control stream (Supplement 1) runs
all four layers together, and the packaged model reproduces it as one file.

Paclitaxel is dosed into `central` (mg) and the CrEL vehicle into
`crel_central` (mL), both intravenously. Outputs are total paclitaxel in plasma
(`Cc`), DRG (`Cdrg`), nerve (`Cpn`) and brain (`Cbrain`), all in ng/mL (tissue
density 1 g/mL), and NfL in serum (`Cnfl_serum`), CSF (`Cnfl_csf`), brain
(`Cnfl_brain`) and DRG + nerve (`Cnfl_pns`) in pg/mL.

# Population

The paclitaxel PK layers were fitted to six data sources (Table I): four
laboratories with individual data in Wistar Hanover and Sprague-Dawley rats and
CD1 mice (57 animals; single IV doses of 2.6 mg/kg, a 5 mg/kg 4-h infusion,
5 mg/kg weekly for 2 or 4 weeks, and 5, 10 or 15 mg/kg three times in week 1
and four times in week 2) plus digitized mean profiles from Nakamura 2016
(Sprague-Dawley rats, 7.5 mg/kg single or weekly for 6 weeks) and Wozniak 2017
(BALB/c mice, 30 mg/kg single or every 2 days x 3 for 2 weeks). The NfL layer
was fitted to a de novo longitudinal study in male Sprague-Dawley rats (8-12
weeks old) given a single 10 mg/kg IV bolus of CrEL-paclitaxel (N = 7) or
saline, and was externally validated against single-time-point sNfL from
sources 2-4. Parameters are referenced to a 0.300 kg rat and scaled
allometrically by body weight; mice differ from rats only by body weight and a
fixed 0.4 g brain weight (`SPECIES_MOUSE = 1`). No between-animal variability
was estimated (all `$OMEGA` fixed to 0), so the packaged model is a
typical-value model with log-scale residual error.

# Simulation helpers

The vehicle dose is not stated in the paper. Paclitaxel Fresenius Kabi
(6 mg/mL, the product used in the NfL study) contains about 527 mg
(about 0.5 mL) of CrEL per mL, so the CrEL dose is taken as 1/12 mL per mg of
paclitaxel (see Assumptions and deviations).

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Ibrahim_2026_paclitaxel_rodent")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "sigma") # the model has no etas

crel_per_mg <- 1 / 12 # mL CrEL per mg paclitaxel (0.5 mL CrEL per 6 mg/mL vial mL)

make_events <- function(dose_mgkg, dose_times, obs_times, wt = 0.3, mouse = 0,
                        id = 1L, dur = 0, crel_ratio = crel_per_mg) {
  amt <- dose_mgkg * wt
  rate_ptx <- if (dur > 0) amt / dur else 0
  rate_crel <- if (dur > 0) amt * crel_ratio / dur else 0
  doses <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = dose_times, amt = amt, rate = rate_ptx, cmt = "central"),
    data.frame(time = dose_times, amt = amt * crel_ratio, rate = rate_crel, cmt = "crel_central")
  )
  doses$evid <- 1L
  obs <- data.frame(time = obs_times, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  # Doses before observations at the same time, so a time-zero observation
  # returns the post-dose concentration.
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = id, WT = wt, SPECIES_MOUSE = mouse) |>
    dplyr::relocate(id, time, amt, rate, evid, cmt, dvid)
}

solve_typ <- function(events) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events, returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE,
                  keep = c("WT", "SPECIES_MOUSE"))
}

grid_10d <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0.01, 1, by = 0.01), seq(1.25, 24, by = 0.25), seq(25, 240, by = 1))))
```

# Baseline NfL steady state

Without paclitaxel, serum and CSF NfL must stay at the Table IV baselines
(Eqs. 13-14).

```{r baseline}
ev_ctl <- make_events(0, dose_times = 0, obs_times = c(0, 24, 120, 240))
sim_ctl <- solve_typ(ev_ctl)
knitr::kable(sim_ctl |> dplyr::select(time, Cnfl_serum, Cnfl_csf, Cnfl_brain, Cnfl_pns),
             digits = 2, caption = "Saline control (typical rat, 0.300 kg).")
stopifnot(
  all(abs(sim_ctl$Cnfl_serum / 17.6446 - 1) < 1e-6),
  all(abs(sim_ctl$Cnfl_csf / 222.501 - 1) < 1e-6)
)
```

# Paclitaxel in plasma and PIPN sites

## Single dose (Figure 4A)

```{r fig4a}
doses <- c(5, 10, 15)
sim_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), function(i) {
  solve_typ(make_events(doses[i], 0, grid_10d, id = i)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose = paste(doses[i], "mg/kg"))
}))

long_ptx <- function(d) {
  d |>
    dplyr::select(dose, time, Plasma = Cc, `Dorsal root ganglia` = Cdrg,
                  `Peripheral nerves` = Cpn, Brain = Cbrain) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(dose, time), names_to = "site", values_to = "conc")
}

ggplot(long_ptx(sim_sd) |> dplyr::filter(time > 0), aes(time / 24, conc, colour = site)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Total PTX conc (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4A of Ibrahim 2026 (typical rat, 0.300 kg).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig4a-check}
day10 <- sim_sd |> dplyr::filter(time == 240, dose == "10 mg/kg")
knitr::kable(day10 |> dplyr::select(time, Cc, Cdrg, Cpn, Cbrain), digits = 2,
             caption = "Typical total paclitaxel 10 days after 10 mg/kg (ng/mL).")
stopifnot(
  # Figure 4A at day 10: DRG > nerve > brain > plasma
  day10$Cdrg > day10$Cpn, day10$Cpn > day10$Cbrain, day10$Cbrain > day10$Cc
)
```

At day 10 the simulated DRG (about 55 ng/mL), nerve (about 9 ng/mL) and plasma
(about 0.2 ng/mL) concentrations match the medians of Figure 4A; brain is
about 6 ng/mL against roughly 2-3 ng/mL in the figure (see Assumptions and
deviations for the dependence on the vehicle dose).

## Repeated dosing (Figure 4B)

Three doses in week 1 and four in week 2, on days 0, 2, 5, 7, 9, 12 and 14
(read from the dashed dosing lines of Figure 4B).

```{r fig4b}
sard_days <- c(0, 2, 5, 7, 9, 12, 14)
grid_30d <- sort(unique(c(0, sard_days * 24 + 0.05, seq(0.25, 720, by = 0.5))))
sim_md <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), function(i) {
  solve_typ(make_events(doses[i], sard_days * 24, grid_30d, id = i)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose = paste(doses[i], "mg/kg"))
}))

ggplot(long_ptx(sim_md) |> dplyr::filter(time > 0), aes(time / 24, conc, colour = site)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sard_days, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Total PTX conc (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4B of Ibrahim 2026.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

After repeated dosing the brain concentration overtakes the nerve concentration
a few days after the last dose, as described in the Results.

## Paclitaxel amounts by sub-compartment (Figure 4C)

```{r fig4c}
amt_sd <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(dose == "10 mg/kg", time > 0) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    time,
    `DRG|Unbound extracellular` = ecf_drg, `DRG|Unbound intracellular` = cu_icf_drg * vicf_drg,
    `DRG|Bound intracellular` = bound_drg, `DRG|Total` = tot_drg,
    `Peripheral nerves|Unbound extracellular` = ecf_pn, `Peripheral nerves|Unbound intracellular` = cu_icf_pn * vicf_pn,
    `Peripheral nerves|Bound intracellular` = bound_pn, `Peripheral nerves|Total` = tot_pn,
    `Brain|Unbound extracellular` = brain_ecf, `Brain|Unbound intracellular` = cu_icf_brain * vicf_brain,
    `Brain|Bound intracellular` = bound_brain, `Brain|Total` = tot_brain
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "key", values_to = "amount_mg") |>
  tidyr::separate(key, into = c("site", "pool"), sep = "\\|")

ggplot(amt_sd, aes(time / 24, amount_mg * 1e9, colour = pool)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~site) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "PTX amount (pg)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4C of Ibrahim 2026 (10 mg/kg single dose).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# NfL kinetics

## Single 10 mg/kg dose against the observed data (Figure 1A-B, Table S1)

```{r nfl-obs}
sim10 <- sim_sd |> dplyr::filter(dose == "10 mg/kg")
nfl_at <- function(t) sim10[sim10$time == t, ]
obs_tab <- data.frame(
  Matrix = c("Serum", "Serum", "Serum", "CSF", "CSF"),
  `Time (h)` = c(0, 72, 240, 72, 240),
  Observed = c("17.6 +/- 7.4 (mean +/- SD)", "335.7 +/- 123.9", "69.3 +/- 28.6",
               "702-783 (range)", "774 (N = 1)"),
  Simulated = c(nfl_at(0)$Cnfl_serum, nfl_at(72)$Cnfl_serum, nfl_at(240)$Cnfl_serum,
                nfl_at(72)$Cnfl_csf, nfl_at(240)$Cnfl_csf),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(obs_tab, digits = 1,
             caption = "NfL (pg/mL) after 10 mg/kg CrEL-paclitaxel. Observed values: Results text and Table S1.")
stopifnot(
  # Results: sNfL at 24 h was more than 60-fold above baseline
  nfl_at(24)$Cnfl_serum > 40 * 17.6446,
  # 72 h serum and CSF inside +/- 50% of the observed centre
  abs(nfl_at(72)$Cnfl_serum / 335.7 - 1) < 0.5,
  abs(nfl_at(72)$Cnfl_csf / 742.5 - 1) < 0.5
)
```

The typical sNfL rises more than 60-fold above baseline in the first day and is
close to the observed mean at 72 h, and CSF NfL at 72 h is near the observed
range. At 240 h the simulated sNfL is about twice the observed mean; the
vehicle-dose sensitivity below shows how much of that depends on the assumed
CrEL dose.

## NfL in serum, CSF, nerves and brain (Figure 1D)

```{r fig1d}
nfl_long <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  dplyr::select(dose, time, Serum = Cnfl_serum, CSF = Cnfl_csf,
                `Peripheral nerves` = Cnfl_pns, Brain = Cnfl_brain) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(dose, time), names_to = "site", values_to = "nfl")
ggplot(nfl_long, aes(time / 24, nfl, colour = site)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "NfL (pg/mL)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 1D of Ibrahim 2026 (single dose, typical rat).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## External-validation regimen (Figure 1C)

```{r fig1c}
ggplot(sim_md |> dplyr::filter(time > 0), aes(time / 24, Cnfl_serum)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Serum NfL (pg/mL)",
       caption = "Compare Figure 1C of Ibrahim 2026 (source 4 regimen, typical rat).")
```

The paper reports that the model underpredicts the day-20 sNfL observed after
15 mg/kg on this schedule (Figure 1C), which the authors attribute to
mechanisms beyond tubulin binding.

# Mouse

The same model predicts mouse PK through body weight and the fixed mouse brain
weight; the NfL layer was fitted to rats only.

```{r mouse}
sim_mouse <- solve_typ(make_events(30, 0, c(0, 1, 6, 24, 72, 168), wt = 0.025, mouse = 1))
knitr::kable(sim_mouse |> dplyr::select(time, Cc, Cdrg, Cpn, Cbrain), digits = 2,
             caption = "Typical 25 g mouse after 30 mg/kg IV (compare the Wozniak 2017 panels of Figure S1).")
```

Plasma at 6 and 24 h is close to the digitized Wozniak 2017 points of Figure
S1A (roughly 200-300 and 2-5 ng/mL). The sciatic-nerve values at 3 and 7 days
are near the observed points of Figure S1B (roughly 100 and 70 ng/g) but above
the paper's fitted line there, which again points to the vehicle dose (next
section).

# Sensitivity to the assumed CrEL dose

```{r crel-sensitivity}
ratios <- c(`1/48` = 1 / 48, `1/24` = 1 / 24, `1/12 (used)` = 1 / 12)
sens <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(ratios), function(nm) {
  rat <- solve_typ(make_events(10, 0, c(72, 240), crel_ratio = ratios[[nm]]))
  mouse <- solve_typ(make_events(30, 0, 168, wt = 0.025, mouse = 1, crel_ratio = ratios[[nm]]))
  data.frame(
    ratio = nm,
    snfl72 = rat$Cnfl_serum[rat$time == 72],
    snfl240 = rat$Cnfl_serum[rat$time == 240],
    brain240 = rat$Cbrain[rat$time == 240],
    drg240 = rat$Cdrg[rat$time == 240],
    mouse_pn168 = mouse$Cpn
  )
}))
sens |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `CrEL (mL per mg paclitaxel)` = ratio, `Rat sNfL 72 h (pg/mL)` = snfl72,
    `Rat sNfL 240 h (pg/mL)` = snfl240, `Rat brain PTX 240 h (ng/mL)` = brain240,
    `Rat DRG PTX 240 h (ng/mL)` = drg240, `Mouse nerve PTX 168 h (ng/g)` = mouse_pn168
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical rat (10 mg/kg) and mouse (30 mg/kg) outputs by assumed vehicle dose.")
```

Lower vehicle doses bring the 240 h sNfL and the brain paclitaxel closer to the
observed mean and to Figure 4A but pull the 72 h sNfL below its observed mean
(335.7 pg/mL); the data do not single out one ratio. The formulation-based value is kept rather than
choosing a ratio to fit a figure.

# PKNCA validation

The paper does not report NCA results, so plasma NCA is checked against the
model's own cumulative AUC state (`auc_central`, which drives the tubulin
binding capacity), a closed-form check of the same simulated profile.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  # each single-subject solve drops its id column, so re-key by dose
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = dose, id = match(dose, paste(doses, "mg/kg"))) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1:3, treatment = paste(doses, "mg/kg"), time = 0,
                      dose = doses * 0.3)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 240, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

auc_state <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 240) |>
  dplyr::transmute(treatment = dose, auc_model = auc_central * 1000)
nca_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(nca_wide, auc_state, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auclast / auc_model - 1))
nca_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, cmax, auclast, auc_model, pct_diff, half.life) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Dose = treatment, `Cmax (ng/mL)` = cmax, `AUC0-240 PKNCA (ng*h/mL)` = auclast,
    `AUC0-240 model state (ng*h/mL)` = auc_model, `Difference (%)` = pct_diff,
    `t1/2 (h)` = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Plasma NCA (typical rat, single dose).")
stopifnot(all(abs(nca_cmp$pct_diff) < 3))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **CrEL vehicle dose.** The model needs the CrEL dose (mL) as a separate input
  into `crel_central`, but the paper does not state it. The simulations here
  use 1/12 mL CrEL per mg paclitaxel, from the composition of the 6 mg/mL
  paclitaxel concentrate (about 527 mg, about 0.5 mL, of CrEL per mL); diluting
  the concentrate with saline does not change the ratio. Several outputs are
  sensitive to this choice because total plasma paclitaxel, the cumulative AUC
  driving tubulin binding, and the CrEL-bound fraction crossing the barriers
  all scale with CrEL; the sensitivity table above quantifies the effect. The
  Figure 4 simulations used the dosing solution of source 4, whose composition
  is not reported. A user simulating a different formulation should supply its
  own CrEL dose.
* **Equations 13-14 in amounts.** The printed Eq. 14 sets
  `kout,csf = kout,serum x NfL_baseline,serum / NfL_baseline,csf` with
  concentrations; the published control stream uses the baseline amounts
  (concentration x 5 mL serum and x 0.25 mL CSF), which is what keeps serum at
  its baseline. The packaged model follows the control stream.
* **Units taken from the control stream.** Table III lists Km_CrEL in mL/h; the
  control stream gives `KMC = 2.57 ;mL/L`, which is dimensionally consistent
  with the Vmax / (Km + C) clearance, and is used here. Kmt and Kd are entered
  in ug/L and converted to mg/L inside the model as in the control stream.
* **No between-animal variability.** All `$OMEGA` entries of the final control
  stream are fixed to 0; the model is typical-value only. The residual errors
  are additive on log-transformed data, encoded as `lnorm()`; the control
  stream adds 1e-6 inside the log, which is omitted.
* **Unused parameters.** `$THETA` 15, 31, 33 (fixed placeholders) and 36 (brain
  NfL residual error; the brain NfL records are ignored in `$DATA`) do not
  enter the model and are not carried.
* **Repeated-dose schedule.** The days of the three-times-weekly then
  four-times-weekly schedule (0, 2, 5, 7, 9, 12, 14) are read from the dashed
  dosing lines of Figure 4B; the paper does not list them.
* **Figure replication is typical-value only.** The published Figure 1D and
  Figure 4 show medians of simulations with parameter uncertainty (SIR); the
  curves here are typical-value predictions without uncertainty.
